briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 launch intensifies US-China frontier race as safety gaps widen

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race has accelerated with multiple frontier releases in June 2026. US labs maintain lead but Chinese models close capability gap rapidly. Regulatory momentum builds globally while prompt injection attacks surge in production deployments.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4 with 2.1T parameters and multimodal reasoning gains. Anthropic's Claude 4 Opus and Google's Gemini 3 Ultra launched within 72 hours. Meta open-sourced Llama 4 while xAI and DeepSeek reported competitive benchmarks on agentic tasks.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines emphasize runtime defenses as red-teaming reveals persistent jailbreaks across leading models.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA ships Blackwell Ultra clusters to Microsoft and Google. Saudi Arabia announces $40B AI data center project. TSMC reports record AI chip orders for Q3 2026 amid global power constraints.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will multi-agent protocol-level security like DialectForge become mandatory for autonomous systems before 2028?
